description: The supplied image is not a scientific figure. It is a small square publisher badge — the "Check for updates" (CrossRef) icon — consisting of a red open-book glyph enclosed by a broken circular arrow rendered in light blue and yellow, with the words "Check for updates" set in two lines of dark grey sans-serif text beneath it, on a white/light-grey background with a thin grey border along the top and left. There are no axes, no units, no scale bars, no legends, no data points, no micrographs, no spectra and no sample labels anywhere in the image. It is a decorative/marketing element exported alongside the article, not a data panel; it therefore cannot be decomposed into (a)/(b)/(c) sub-figures and carries no information about the Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C (x = 4, 6, 8, 10) low-density steels described in the paper title and abstract. Consequently, no microstructure, phase-evolution, Al-content or tensile-property evidence can be visualised, and nothing in this image supports or contradicts the paper's claims about the austenite-to-ferrite-based duplex transition with increasing Al content. Any text agent using this figure group should treat it as empty of scientific content and rely on other figure groups for evidence.
